messages:
maya: Quick flag — after we tightened egress/netpols in the private VPC yesterday, a handful of onprem customers reported inference failures. Saw repeated KMS denies for the keystore proxy service account.

 sam: Can you paste the error? which SA?

 maya: Logs from the proxy: `2026-03-21T09:14:22Z ERROR decrypt failed: AccessDeniedException: user: arn:aws:sts::...:assumed-role/segnet-proxy/webhook not authorized for kms:Decrypt`

 sam: that looks like RBAC + KMS policy mismatch. We tightened pod egress/egress-allowlist so the proxy maybe hitting a different NAT path/role. Did we roll out the service-account change last night?

 maya: We did switch the proxy to use `segnet-proxy-sa` (per security request) and removed a legacy `proxy-legacy` binding.

 tasha: Two quick hypotheses: 1) KMS key policy doesn't include the new role/principal; 2) network path to the KMS proxy/hsm is disrupted and IAM condition failed (source IP/cert mismatch).

 kevin: Also check the keystore agent's token audience header — we had an issue months ago where a rotated kube-apiserver cert broke STS-based role assumption.

 sam: Replication steps I ran: `kubectl -n priv get pods -l app=segnet-proxy -o wide` then `kubectl exec -it segnet-proxy-abc -- tail -n 200 /var/log/proxy.log`. Confirmed the AccessDenied from KMS, and `curl -s http://169.254.169.254` from the pod times out on some nodes.

 maya: Interesting — some nodes still reach IMDS, others time out. That correlates with the new netpol which restricts hostNetwork: true pods to a control-plane-only route.

 tasha: For mitigation I suggest: 1) Add a short-lived exception in the netpol for segnet-proxy pods to reach IMDS/KMS endpoints, 2) Update the KMS key policy to include the ARN for the new assumed role (segnet-proxy role), 3) Enable more verbose audit logging for decrypt attempts so we can triage.

 kevin: I can push a targeted netpol patch (10m). If we do that, we should also add an audit log annotation to the pod (so logs show the SA). Something like: `kubectl annotate pod segnet-proxy-abc redwood/security-audit=segnet-proxy-sa` — then our log shipper tags it.

 maya: Please hold on the netpol patch until we confirm KMS policy. If key policy is missing the principal, opening the net is unnecessary and risky.

 sam: Agreed. Maya, can you paste the KMS key policy lines? I can run a dry check against the assumed role ARN.

 maya: Pasted snippet (sanitized): `{ "Sid": "AllowOldProxyRole", "Principal": { "AWS": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/proxy-legacy" }, "Action": "kms:Decrypt" }` — no entry for the new role.

 tasha: There's the problem. KMS denies because key policy only allows the legacy role. We need to add the new role ARN or a condition that matches `sts:AssumedRole` session tags for `segnet-proxy-sa`.

 kevin: I'll open a PR to append the new principal to the key policy and include an audit comment. Also will prepare a netpol rollback/exception as a follow-up if needed.

 maya: Good. Also add a short playbook note: when rotating service accounts, update KMS key policies and audit IAM role mappings before netpol tightening. We should automate a policy-check in our preflight CI for private deploys.

 sam: For immediate customer impact: recommend a scoped key policy update (minimal grant) + notify affected tenants. If any tenant requires FIPS/HSM constraints, route through security for approval first.

 deploy-bot: deploy started by kevin: branch/kevin/kms-policy-add (sha: abc123) — CI passed, applying to staging then prod in 5m.

 security-bot: Alert: change to KMS key policy will be recorded in audit-log stream `priv-kms-updates`. Make sure to include justification ticket number.

 maya: Action items: kevin -> PR and apply key policy update (ETA 20m). sam -> add audit logging for decrypt failures and collect last 48h for affected nodes (ETA 1h). tasha -> draft short rollback netpol patch if needed (ETA 30m). maya -> notify customers and legal (ETA 30m).

 kevin: On it. Will paste PR link and policy diff once live.

 maya: Thanks all. Keep replies in-thread; we'll escalate to incident channel if we see more denies after policy apply. :thumbsup:
